# Scenario X01 — Enterprise Customer Demands a Bespoke Feature

**Domain:** B2B enterprise. **Situation:** conflicting stakeholders, customer pressure.

## Context

A mid-market SaaS product ("Pulse," a CRM analytics tool) has a large enterprise customer
that accounts for roughly 12% of ARR. Their executive sponsor is asking for a bespoke
reporting module ("portfolio dashboards") that only they would use as designed. The sales
executive on the account wants to say yes to protect the renewal. Engineering estimates the
module is 4–6 months of dedicated work that would displace two roadmap items. The product
strategy (written last quarter) says the company focuses on self-serve analytics for SMBs and
does not do custom development.

## Inputs available (imperfect)

- The renewal is not at risk on its current terms; the customer has not threatened to leave.
- Two other enterprise accounts have asked for the same thing "if you build it, we'll buy it"
  — neither is under contract.
- No win/loss analysis exists for this customer.
- The two displaced roadmap items target 40+ self-serve customers.
- No cost-to-serve or support-burden estimate for a bespoke module exists.

## Ask

You have one page to recommend whether to build the bespoke module, defer it, or decline it,
and what you would do next. State your reasoning and any evidence you are relying on or
missing.
